options.label: Reject All Bids and Re-bid
options.description: Reject all current bids for Bid No. 26-04 to avoid void contract risks and political bias claims, then issue a new invitation to bid with stricter licensing specifications.

options.label: Award to Second-Lowest Bidder (Tasker & Moye)
options.description: Immediately award the contract to Tasker & Moye as the second-lowest bidder based on their claimed qualifications, bypassing further verification of their subcontractors.

options.label: Conditional Award with Cure Period
options.description: Award the contract to the lowest bidder (Corvane) conditionally, requiring them to provide proof of licensed subcontractors or cure the Addendum 2 acknowledgment within 24–48 hours before final execution.

options.label: Split Scope Award (Dual Prime)
options.description: Reject the single prime contract structure and instead issue two separate contracts: one for general building work awarded to Corvane and another for specialized systems (HVAC/Electrical/Fire) awarded to a qualified specialist or Tasker & Moye.

options.label: Pre-Award Cure via Responsibility Hearing
options.description: Classify the lowest bidder's issue as a 'responsibility defect' rather than 'nonresponsiveness,' hold a hearing to find them not responsible, and grant a conditional award allowing them to execute binding agreements with licensed subcontractors within 48 hours prior to signing.

options.label: Reject All Bids and Re-bid
options.note: This is a legally defensible exercise of the agency's broad discretion to reject all bids if specifications are flawed, but it catastrophically fails the client's schedule goals by pushing the project timeline back by months, missing the critical December 1 switchgear deadline.

options.label: Award to Second-Lowest Bidder (Tasker & Moye)
options.note: This is unlawful because it bypasses the mandatory statutory process for determining responsibility, as the agency cannot simply skip to the second bidder without first providing the lowest bidder notice and a hearing to address the specific defects in their bid.

options.label: Conditional Award with Cure Period
options.note: This is a risky legal maneuver that attempts to shortcut the responsibility hearing process by imposing a cure period, which courts may set aside as an improper attempt to waive statutory licensing requirements without a formal record, though it best serves the client's schedule and cost interests.

options.label: Split Scope Award (Dual Prime)
options.note: This is legally risky and likely to be set aside as a material deviation from the original Invitation to Bid that fundamentally altered the scope and risk allocation without a new bidding process, while also failing the client's goal of a single point of responsibility.

options.label: Pre-Award Cure via Responsibility Hearing
options.note: This is the only legally sound option that respects due process by treating the licensing and subcontractor issues as responsibility defects requiring a formal hearing, though it only partly serves the client by introducing a delay that threatens the immediate schedule.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately recognized that the 'nonresponsiveness' label is a trap for the licensing issue and would have advised holding the recommendation until the bidder's written response is received to determine if the defect is curable or requires a formal responsibility hearing, rather than proposing a Monday morning decision.
grade.overall: The consultation correctly identifies the legal pitfalls of rejecting a bid without a hearing but fails to prioritize the mandatory waiting period for the bidder's response as the critical first step, leading to recommendations that either violate due process or ignore the statutory requirements for specialty licensing.
